sentences.text: This creature possessed teeth in its jaw and branchial spines on its gill arches — the bony supports for gills.
The species is known only from fossils found in the Lower Devonian Hunsrück slate of Germany.
It is often considered a relative of the order Pseudopetalichthyida and a basal placoderm.
It is tentatively classified as one of the most basal placoderms based on shoulder joint similarities.
Stensioella lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
Paleontologist Philippe Janvier suggests that Stensioella was a holocephalid rather than a placoderm.
